summary: The same-noise lower comparison is false for an admissible additive-noise example. Its noise sign can be repaired locally. The all-time convolution estimate also fails, while its short-time restriction suffices for the inspected critical doubling argument.

problem_checks.reason: The original equation and common-noise quantifier agree with the report. Setting w=-v_- gives coefficient -sigma(w), whereas u has +sigma(u); localization cannot change that mismatch. For sigma=1, u0=0 and alpha=4 all real assumptions hold, and v=v_- pathwise before stopping. Under the finite-energy constant control h=-4096 up to T=3/16384, u_h=-at and v_h>=1-at>=1/4. Therefore integral v_h^(-4)<=256T=3/64, v_h(T)<=19/64 and u_h(T)+v_h(T)<=-29/64.
problem_checks.positive_probability_check: The control has squared L2 norm 6144*pi. The one-dimensional additive periodic stochastic convolution is a continuous centered Gaussian field on the compact cylinder, so its Cameron-Martin image Z_h lies in its support, as in the retained Hairer Theorem 4.44 and Exercise 4.46. For the mass-one semigroup, local drift Lipschitz constant L=4*8^5 on [1/8,infinity) gives sup|v-v_h|<=delta*exp(L*T). Choose delta so this is <1/16 and sup|u-u_h|<1/16. The controlled lower bound 1/4 then keeps both auxiliaries above 1/8, their finite upper bound stays below 2, and the strict comparison margin remains negative. Thus the violation occurs on a positive-probability neighborhood before the actual local stopping boundaries; the deterministic path is not being assigned positive point probability.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_repair: Replacing the lower noise by -sigma(-v_-)W gives w coefficient +sigma(w) and negative drift -f(-w)<=0. Local Lipschitzness, growth, absolute-value and squared-coefficient estimates are retained. Standard localized comparison then gives the intended lower envelope, conditional on the external comparison theorem. The original proposition is explicitly a core step of the Theorem 3.3-to-1.1 reduction; Major is supported without asserting global-existence falsity.
problem_checks.normalization_scope: The review consistently checks the mass-one semigroup of the stated heat equation; its separate kernel normalization clarification is supported by the original mass-one calculation on page 11. It is not used as an extra substantive Problem.
problem_checks.verification_method: independent analytic sign transformation, exact rational control bounds, Gaussian-support and stopped-continuity argument; original arithmetic output reused without rerun

problem_checks.reason: For deterministic adapted phi=1, the required p-integral is 2*pi*T. The mass-one periodic kernel leaves a Brownian spatial average with variance T/(2*pi); spatial averaging therefore yields a positive-constant lower bound T^(p/2) for the displayed supremum moment. The claimed upper bound grows only T^(p/4-1/2), so its ratio is T^(p/4+1/2) and is unbounded for every p>6. The source explicitly asserts time-independent Cp, and its nondecaying zero mode contradicts the all-time t^(-1/2) kernel bound. The printed constant rescaling of the kernel changes constants, not this contradiction.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_repair: For 0<T<=1, the periodic heat-kernel estimates are uniform. The source factorization interval 3/(2p)<beta<1/4 is nonempty exactly when p>6; the powers beta*p-3/2 and p/4-p*beta add to p/4-3/2. At fixed M, the actual horizons T_m=C^2*M^2*2^(-2m+6) tend to zero, so increasing m0 imposes T_m<=1 without changing the level-exponent cancellation. Thus the false unused all-time uniformity is Minor rather than a demonstrated additional central failure.
problem_checks.verification_method: independent analytic zero-mode and scaling calculation with direct inspection of source hypotheses and later application

limitations: Acceptance checks the two reported Problems, their assumptions, positive-probability argument, local corrections, severity and actual central dependencies; it is not a repeated full-paper review.
Only exact arXiv:2309.04330v1 was scientifically compared. No equivalence with the journal Version of Record or journal-final error is asserted.
The supporting Hairer reference is restricted to pages 31-32; the comparison and singular-positivity theorems are not re-proved.
